Gregory Gioro | Backpacking South America on Instagram: "Day 355 of 365: Moldova—one of Europe’s least visited countries. Many who have heard of it may dismiss it as Romania, and indeed, there are those who support the unification of Moldova and Romania. From the outside looking in, the two countries share a very important bond: they are the only two countries in Europe that speak Romanian. But if history has taught me anything, it’s that it’s never simple. Over the centuries, Moldova and Romania have been governed as part of one territory, but they’ve also spent some formative time apart.

After Romania declared its independence from the Ottoman Empire, it ceded the area of present-day Moldova to the Russian Empire in exchange for access to the Black Sea. Thus, Moldova spent much of the 1800s as a part of the Russia, during which time it was called Bessarabia. After the fall of tsarist Russia in the early 1900s, Bessarabia was taken back by Romania, only to be ceded later to the Soviet Union, which organized the territory (along with bits of Ukraine) into the Soviet Socialist Republic of Moldova.

This history of being ping-ponged between two nations explains—at least partially—the duality of Moldova, where, on the streets of Chișinău, signs can be found in Russian, buses are imported from Belarus, and a never-ending flock of shawled babushkas can be seen everywhere you go.
.
.
.
#moldova #visitmoldova #moldavia #chisinau #visitchisinau #easterneurope @moldova.travel"
